stem: Which record correctly separates plan from reality?
choices: Record the work-order target EC separately from the actual EC measured on the identified sample.
Copy the target EC into the measured-value field so the record shows the intended condition.
Keep only the target because planned values are more important than one observation.
Record only “normal” if the measured value was close to target.
rationale: Plan and reality should remain distinct. The target EC shows what the work order intended; the measured EC shows what the identified sample actually contained. Keeping both values separate makes deviations visible and preserves a reconstructable record.
